__inputs.name: DS_PROMETHEUS
__inputs.label: Prometheus
__inputs.description: Pick the Prometheus that scrapes vlpds /metrics

title: vlpds
description: vlpds PDS for its operator: is it up, who uses it, sign-in security, what they post, how it federates, moderation, email, resources and cost. Engineers: the 'vlpds internals' dashboard. Generated by bench/obs/grafana/gen_dashboard.py (also printed by `vlpds dashboards`).

links.title: Internals dashboard
links.tooltip: The engineer's view: every subsystem, for debugging

links.title: Runbook
links.tooltip: What each alert means and what to do

panels.title: Is my PDS up and serving people well?
PDS status
panels.description: Down: no server is answering. Degraded: a server is down, over 5% of requests are failing, an urgent alert is firing, or part of the data has no server. Otherwise working normally.

targets.expr: (clamp_max(count(up{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster"} == 1), 1) or vector(0)) * (2 - clamp_max((count((up{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster"} == 0) and on (instance) group by (instance) (last_over_time(vlpds_build_info{cluster=~"$cluster"}[1h]))) or vector(0)) + ((sum(rate(vlpds_http_requests_total{cluster=~"$cluster", status=~"5.."}[5m])) or vector(0)) / sum(rate(vlpds_http_requests_total{cluster=~"$cluster"}[5m])) > bool 0.05 or vector(0)) + (count(ALERTS{alertstate="firing", alertname=~"Vlpds.*", severity="page", cluster=~"$cluster"}) or vector(0)) + (abs(max(vlpds_shard_layout_shards{cluster=~"$cluster"}) - (sum(vlpds_owned_partitions{cluster=~"$cluster"}) or vector(0))) or vector(0)), 1))

panels.title: Served without error (24 h)
panels.description: Share of all requests over the last day that did not fail on the server side (5xx): what your users experienced, Bluesky app requests passed through included.

panels.title: Failing requests right now
panels.description: Share of requests in the last 5 minutes that failed on the server side. Red at 5%: the 'Many requests are failing' alert.

panels.title: Bluesky app working
panels.description: Share of your users' Bluesky app requests (timelines, threads, notifications, profiles) that the Bluesky AppView answered, over 15 minutes. Errors here are the AppView's or the network's, not your server's, but your users see them.

panels.title: Servers online
panels.description: vlpds servers answering monitoring, and those that answered within the last hour but don't now.

targets.expr: count((up{job=~"$job", cluster=~"$cluster"} == 0) and on (instance) group by (instance) (last_over_time(vlpds_build_info{cluster=~"$cluster"}[1h]))) or vector(0)

panels.title: Cluster health
panels.description: Behind the scenes: green when all of your users' data is being served by a running server and no urgent alert fires. Red: open the internals dashboard (link in this panel's menu) and the runbook.

targets.expr: clamp_max((abs(max(vlpds_shard_layout_shards{cluster=~"$cluster"}) - (sum(vlpds_owned_partitions{cluster=~"$cluster"}) or vector(0))) or vector(0)) + (count(ALERTS{alertstate="firing", alertname=~"Vlpds.*", severity="page", cluster=~"$cluster"}) or vector(0)), 1)

panels.title: Requests per minute, by outcome
panels.description: Everything your PDS answered: apps, relays, the Bluesky app's requests passed through. Some refused requests are normal (expired sign-ins, missing records); failures should be near zero.

targets.legendFormat: refused (bad request, not signed in, not found)

matcher.options: refused (bad request, not signed in, not found)

panels.title: How long common actions take (95% finish within)
panels.description: 95th percentile over 15 minutes: 95 of 100 requests were at least this fast. Posting includes saving durably; sign-in includes the deliberately slow password check; the Bluesky app line is the AppView's time to answer. Dashed at 1 s, where people start to notice.

panels.title: Accounts
panels.description: Accounts hosted here by status: exact, kept up to date with every account change, each server reporting the share it holds right now (while a server is down, its share is missing until another server takes its accounts over, within seconds). Deactivated accounts were paused by their owner; taken down / suspended ones by a moderator.

panels.title: Accounts that posted or changed something
panels.description: Accounts with any new post, like, follow, profile change etc. in the window (your active users), counted in whole UTC days: "last day" is yesterday and today, "last week" the last 7 days and today, so each covers up to one day more than its name. Exact otherwise, kept up to date with every write. People who only read don't show here; see Sign-ins.

panels.title: Sign-ups (24 h)
panels.description: Accounts created in the last day, and sign-up attempts refused (bad invite code, blocked email domain, reserved handle, handle taken...). Breakdown: Sign-ups and account changes.

panels.title: Sign-ins (24 h)
panels.description: Successful sign-ins (password, app password or the sign-in page apps open) in the last day, and failed ones (wrong password or wrong 2FA code). Apps stay signed in for weeks, so this counts new sign-ins, not everyone using the PDS.

panels.title: Sign-ups and account changes per hour
panels.description: Each point counts the hour before it. Refusal reasons: invite (missing or used-up invite code), email_policy (disposable or unsupported email), handle_policy (reserved or offensive handle), taken (handle or email in use), invalid (other bad input), error (server problem). Account changes: deactivated / reactivated by the owner, deleted.

panels.title: Sign-ins per hour
panels.description: Password, app-password and sign-in-page (OAuth) sign-ins, each point counting the hour before it. Lots of wrong passwords from one place get blocked by rate limits (purple). Refused because of the account's own settings: the owner chose 'OAuth only' or turned app passwords off.

properties.value: app password refused (turned off by the owner)

panels.title: Second step at sign-in (24 h)
panels.description: Successful sign-ins in the last day by their second step: a code from an authenticator app, a code sent by email, a browser the user chose to trust (it skips the code for --trusted-device-days), or none (no two-factor sign-in set up, or an app password, which never asks for one).

panels.title: New-device alerts (24 h)
panels.description: Sign-ins from a device an account hadn't used before, and whether the owner was emailed about it. Each account gets at most 3 a day. Held back: an email limit (per address, per server or for the whole PDS) was spent, so the user wasn't told.

panels.title: Accounts scheduled for deletion
panels.description: Deactivated accounts whose owner (or an app they allowed) asked for them to be deleted later. They're deleted once that date and at least 3 days of deactivation have passed; reactivating cancels it. Taken-down accounts wait until the takedown is reversed. As of each server's last check (every 10 minutes).

panels.title: Sign-ins by second step, per hour
panels.description: Successful sign-ins by their second step, and browsers users chose to trust, each point counting the hour before it.

panels.title: Account protection changes, per hour
panels.description: Users changing their Security settings (OAuth only, blocking app passwords, new-sign-in emails), removing trusted browsers, and sign-ins those settings refused (oauth_required: the main password outside the sign-in page; app_passwords_blocked). Each point counts the hour before it.

panels.title: Account deletions per hour
panels.description: Accounts deleted, by who asked, each point counting the hour before it; and accounts waiting for a scheduled deletion (right, dashed). A sudden jump in scheduled accounts is the 'Many accounts were just scheduled for deletion' alert: you have at least 3 days to look.

panels.title: App permissions, per hour
panels.description: What users answered when an app asked for access (all it asked for, some of it, or no), and requests an app or a limited app password made beyond what it was allowed (403). The latter is usually an app asking for more than it should, not an attack. Each point counts the hour before it.

panels.title: Created in the last 24 h
panels.description: New posts, likes, reposts and follows your users made in the last day (deletions not subtracted), images and videos they uploaded, and the uploads' total size.

panels.title: Created per hour, by type
panels.description: Posts, likes, follows and everything else your users created, by type, each point counting the hour before it. 'Other apps' are records of non-Bluesky apps (e.g. other atproto apps your users use).

panels.title: Media uploads per hour
panels.description: Uploads per hour by kind (left) and their total size (right, dashed).

panels.title: Firehose subscribers
panels.description: Relays and other services following your PDS's live update stream (the 'firehose'), on every server. 0 means the network isn't hearing about new posts: check requestCrawl below. The operator console's Firehose page lists who they are.

panels.title: Relays dropped for falling behind (24 h)
panels.description: Relays cut off because they read updates too slowly. They reconnect and catch up; repeated drops mean that relay (or its network) can't keep up.

panels.title: Delay before relays see new posts
panels.description: 99% of new posts, likes, etc. reached the relay stream within this time after being saved (15 min).

panels.title: Last crawl request accepted
panels.description: How long ago a relay accepted your PDS's requestCrawl ('please follow me'), sent at startup to --crawlers and by 'vlpds admin request-crawl'. Failed attempts are in Directory and identity.

panels.title: PLC directory errors (24 h)
panels.description: Failed calls to the PLC directory (plc.directory), which publishes your users' identities. While it fails, sign-ups and handle changes fail.

panels.title: Directory and identity, per hour
panels.description: Identity updates announced to the network (identity: new account or handle change; account: status change), PLC directory calls by result (rejected / unavailable are failures), custom-domain handle lookups, the account page's checks of a new handle (available / taken for a name here; verified / unverified for the user's own domain), and requestCrawl calls to relays (rejected / failed are failures).

panels.title: Firehose subscribers over time
panels.description: Relays and other services connected to the firehose, and how many of them are reading old updates from storage (they asked to start from a point in the past) before they get new ones live.

panels.title: Firehose connects, disconnects and refusals, per hour
panels.description: Firehose connections per hour by how they started and how they ended. A few drops a day are normal (relays restart and reconnect). The same relay dropped for falling behind again and again can't keep up.

properties.value: connected (from a point in the past)
refused: asked to start in the future
refused: too many connections from one address

panels.title: Firehose: events/s per connection vs this PDS
panels.description: Updates per second each connection gets (5 min average), against the updates your PDS puts on its firehose (the bold line). A connection that's keeping up sits on the bold line. One below it for long is falling behind. Lines are named relay (when it's one you list in --crawlers), address and connection number (#conn, as the console's Firehose page shows it). Past 1,000 connections on a server the rest are one line, other.

panels.title: Reports and takedowns (24 h)
panels.description: Reports your users filed (on posts, accounts...) and passed to the moderation service (failed: the service refused or couldn't be reached), and takedowns applied by you or your moderation service (com.atproto.admin.updateSubjectStatus), and reversals.

panels.title: Abusive traffic blocked (24 h)
panels.description: Requests refused for coming too fast (rate limits), plus connections refused from one address opening too many, plus one account flooding the Bluesky app proxy.

targets.expr: (round(sum (increase(vlpds_rate_limited_total{cluster=~"$cluster"}[1d]))) or vector(0)) + (round(sum (increase(vlpds_firehose_rejected_total{cluster=~"$cluster"}[1d]))) or vector(0)) + (round(sum (increase(vlpds_proxy_rejected_total{cluster=~"$cluster"}[1d]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Emails (24 h)
panels.description: Emails sent (address confirmation, password reset, sign-in codes, account deletion...) and ones that could not be delivered. Failures mean users can't confirm, reset or sign in with 2FA codes.

panels.title: Blocked and refused, per hour
panels.description: Abusive or excessive traffic your PDS turned away, each point counting the hour before it. Sign-ups blocked by policy: invite (no or bad invite code), email_policy (disposable email), handle_policy (reserved or offensive handle).

targets.legendFormat: too many relay connections from one address
one account flooding the app proxy

panels.title: Emails per hour
panels.description: Emails sent by kind, and ones that failed or were dropped (red), each point counting the hour before it.

panels.title: Busiest server: CPU and memory in use
panels.description: On the busiest server: CPU used out of the cores available to vlpds (5 min; sustained over 70% leaves little headroom for spikes), and memory used out of what the server or its container allows (85% and 95% are the memory alerts; at 100% the server is killed and restarts).

panels.title: Disk cache
panels.description: Local disk cache (--cache-dir) used out of its size limit (the cache's own count of its files). It saves storage requests; full is normal (oldest entries make room).

panels.title: Estimated storage request bill
panels.description: ESTIMATE: object-storage request charges for a month at the last hour's request rate, at the Class A (writes, lists) and Class B (reads) prices picked at the top (S3 or R2 list prices; R2's free tier and S3's free deletes are not subtracted, so the real bill can be lower). Storage space and data transfer are not included. A one-account PDS is about $2-5/month on S3 and $0 on R2.

panels.title: CPU and memory by server
panels.description: Per server: CPU used out of its available cores, and memory used out of its limit.

targets.expr: (sum by (instance) (rate(vlpds_process_cpu_seconds_total{cluster=~"$cluster"}[5m])) / on (instance) max by (instance) (vlpds_cpu_cores{cluster=~"$cluster"})) * on (instance) group_left (node_id) max by (instance, node_id) (vlpds_build_info{cluster=~"$cluster"})

(max by (instance) (vlpds_process_resident_bytes{cluster=~"$cluster"}) / on (instance) max by (instance) (vlpds_memory_limit_bytes{cluster=~"$cluster"})) * on (instance) group_left (node_id) max by (instance, node_id) (vlpds_build_info{cluster=~"$cluster"})

panels.title: Storage requests and estimated monthly cost
panels.description: Object-store requests per second by price class (left) and what the last hour's rate would cost over a month (right, dashed; an estimate, see the bill stat).

panels.title: Alerts firing now
panels.description: Alerts from the PDS's alert rules (ops/alerts.yml), in plain words. 'urgent' (page) means users are or soon will be affected; 'soon' (ticket) means look at it today. Empty = nothing firing, or the alert rules aren't loaded. Each alert's fix is in the runbook. Needs ops/alerts.yml loaded in the rule evaluator that writes ALERTS to this Prometheus; without it this stays empty ([monitoring docs](https://github.com/jazware/vlpds/blob/main/docs/operations/monitoring.md)).

targets.expr: max by (alertname, severity, instance) (ALERTS{alertstate="firing", alertname=~"Vlpds.*", cluster=~"$cluster"})

VlpdsNodeFailStopped.text: A server stopped itself to protect data

VlpdsPeerPresumedDead.text: A server lost contact with another

VlpdsIncompatibleNode.text: A server's version is too old to run

VlpdsShardsUnowned.text: Part of the data is not being served

VlpdsShardsOverOwned.text: Part of the data is claimed twice

VlpdsOwnershipImbalanced.text: Work is unevenly spread over servers

VlpdsShardOpenErrors.text: A server failed to load data

VlpdsTakeoverReplaySlow.text: Recovery after a server failure was slow

VlpdsLeaseRenewalNearCeiling.text: A server's heartbeat to storage is slow

VlpdsLeaseRenewalAtCeiling.text: A server's heartbeat to storage is too slow (it may stop)

VlpdsLeaseValidityLow.text: A server nearly missed its heartbeat

VlpdsCommitLatencyCritical.text: Saving posts is very slow (writes may fail)

VlpdsWatermarkLagHigh.text: A server's clock or storage is lagging

VlpdsProxyAccountCapSustained.text: One account is flooding the Bluesky app proxy

VlpdsWriteInternalErrors.text: Posts are failing with server errors

VlpdsForwardLatencyHigh.text: Servers are slow to reach each other

VlpdsWriteResendsSustained.text: Posts are being retried a lot

VlpdsFirehoseEmitDelayCritical.text: Relays get new posts very late

VlpdsFirehoseConsumersTooSlow.text: Relays are being dropped for falling behind

VlpdsFirehoseMergeSpilling.text: Relay feed is under memory pressure

VlpdsObjectStoreBrownout.text: Storage is failing for several servers (outage risk)

VlpdsSlateDbL0Stalls.text: Database writes are being held back

VlpdsReplayBacklogHigh.text: Recovery after a crash would be slow

VlpdsRetentionNotRunning.text: Old data cleanup is not running

VlpdsDeadLogUnfenced.text: A stopped server's data is not cleaned up

VlpdsReshardGcFailing.text: Cleanup after data moves is failing

VlpdsForcedDetachFailing.text: Cleanup after data moves keeps failing

VlpdsMemoryHigh.text: A server is running low on memory

VlpdsMemoryCritical.text: A server is about to run out of memory

VlpdsKeyServiceUnavailable.text: The key service is unreachable (posting fails)

VlpdsSecretUnwrapRejected.text: The key service rejected a key

VlpdsPlcDirectoryUnavailable.text: The PLC directory is unreachable (sign-ups fail)

VlpdsSignatureFaultFailStop.text: A server stopped on bad signatures (replace hardware)

VlpdsLazyMstInvalid.text: An account's data index was rebuilt

VlpdsFirehoseMergeQueueNearBudget.text: Relay feed is near its memory limit

VlpdsRuntimeSaturated.text: A server is out of CPU

VlpdsPeerTlsReloadFailing.text: A server couldn't load its new certificate

VlpdsPeerTlsHandshakeFailures.text: Servers are refusing each other's certificates

VlpdsScheduledDeletionsSurge.text: Many accounts were just scheduled for deletion

VlpdsSignInAlertsSuppressed.text: New sign-in alert emails aren't going out
